extracted.intended_audience: prospective Knight-Hennessy Scholars / prospective Stanford graduate students
extracted.subtask_description: Selection and program expectations for the Knight-Hennessy Scholars fellowship at Stanford University; describes eligibility (Stanford graduate enrollment), the character qualities sought in applicants, and program participation/funding features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Knight-Hennessy scholars are visionary thinkers who are curious, open-minded, analytical, eager for cross-cultural perspective, and genuinely excited to boldly and creatively address our world’s important challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This dimension emphasizes intellectual curiosity, analytical ability, openness to diverse perspectives, and a demonstrated eagerness to address significant global problems with bold, creative thinking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposeful leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Knight-Hennessy scholars are courageous leaders who are ethical, decisive, resilient, driven to achieve meaningful results, and motivated to inspire others to effect positive change at scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators look for ethical decision-making, decisiveness, resilience, a track record or clear motivation for achieving measurable impact, and the ability to mobilize or inspire others toward large-scale positive change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civic mindset
rubrics_metrics.description: Knight-Hennessy scholars are collaborative community members who are humble, empathetic, trustworthy, oriented to act in service of others, and deeply passionate about contributing to the greater good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This dimension values collaboration, humility, empathy, trustworthiness, a demonstrated service orientation, and sustained passion for contributing to societal benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stanford graduate enrollment (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: All scholars are Stanford University graduate students, who join Knight-Hennessy Scholars in addition to enrolling in a graduate degree program at any of Stanford's seven schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be or intend to be enrolled in a Stanford graduate degree program (at one of Stanford’s seven schools) in order to become Knight-Hennessy Scholars; scholarship participation is in addition to the graduate degree program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership development participation (program expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholars participate in up to three years of programming that complements their graduate studies and prepares them to take on leadership roles in academia, industry, government, nonprofits, and the community at large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being a scholar requires active engagement in the program’s multidisciplinary leadership-development activities over the fellowship period; selection implies willingness and capacity to participate in and contribute to cohort programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship funding terms (program feature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholars receive a fellowship for up to three years of tuition, depending upon their degree length. In addition, scholars receive a stipend for living and academic expenses, and a travel stipend for one annual trip to and from Stanford.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This item describes the financial support structure (tuition coverage up to three years, living/academic stipend, annual travel stipend) and is part of program terms rather than a qualitative selection metric, but is relevant for applicant expectations and eligibility planning.
